A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SVL/HSVL research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original SVL/HSVL benchmark experiments, flat-critic comparisons, and architectural ablations in Section 5 and the appendix tables.

after.justification: v2 retains the original SVL/HSVL experimental results, including benchmark evaluations and ablations in Section 5 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The hazard-learning objective, low-rank architecture, finite-horizon/PCH/PCS estimators, flat SVL critic, and hierarchical policy extraction remain unchanged, including Algorithm 1 and Appendix A.3–A.5.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same OGBench coverage: state-based and visual maze navigation/stitching, cube manipulation, and puzzle tasks. Task membership matches throughout the main and appendix tables.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain GCBC, GCIVL, GCIQL, QRL, CRL, and HIQL. Tables 2 and 5 retain the same original and re-evaluated CRL comparisons against SVL.

E3.justification: Evaluation procedures and settings remain unchanged, including the shared depth-6 DDPG+BC actor in Section 5.2 and the training budgets, model configurations, and hyperparameters in Table 3.

E4.justification: Both retain the same critic-isolation experiment, actor/critic depth ablation, and finite-horizon/PCH/PCS comparison. Figures 2–3 and Tables 2, 4, and 5 contain no added or revised analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report results over four seeds using the same mean and standard-deviation conventions. No repeated-run information or uncertainty-estimation procedure changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results and findings match in Tables 1–2 and 4–8 and Figures 2–3. For example, Table 1 retains HSVL's 81±1 versus HIQL's 12±4 on humanoidmaze-giant-navigate-v0.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Proposition 4.1, Lemma 4.2, and Appendix A.1–A.5 proofs and derivations are unchanged. Appendix text reflows across pages without mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The survival formulation, three value estimators, HSVL contribution, and long-horizon performance claims retain the same scope. Removing a redundant Monte Carlo characterization from the introduction leaves that characterization intact elsewhere.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning bootstrap errors, dataset size, and critic versus hierarchy contributions remain unchanged. The sparse-reward applicability boundary, censoring assumptions, and future-work limitations are also retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page hyperlink labeled 'Webpage and code' to the abstract. Implementation details remain unchanged, and Section 5 still promises release upon acceptance; the addition establishes access guidance, not verified code availability.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning remain the same. 'Guided flow policy' changes from an ICLR 2026 citation to its 2025 arXiv entry with different author formatting, but represents the same work.

P1.justification: Localized wording edits affect the abstract, introduction, and related work. Bibliographic metadata and heading capitalization change, and the preprint footer becomes an ICML proceedings notice. The section structure remains intact.

P2.justification: All four figures and eight tables are retained. Caption labels and typography change, some appendix captions become smaller, and text and tables shift slightly. Diagram content, plot displays, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new 'Webpage and code' hyperlink improves resource discoverability, while standardized captions modestly improve presentation consistency. Scientific content and supporting evidence remain unchanged. Section 5 retains future-release wording, so the PDFs do not establish an improvement in actual code availability.
